Pancreatic adenocarcinoma—especially in the head of the pancreas—causes painless obstructive jaundice, weight loss, and fatigue; though typically more acute in jaundice onset, a one-month timeline fits early progression. Autoimmune hepatitis overlaps clinically and biochemically with PBC and can present with fatigue, weight loss, and jaundice, particularly in seronegative or overlap syndromes. Cholangiocarcinoma (especially distal or hilar) is nearly as likely, given similar presentation and obstructive physiology. Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is plausible in younger patients or those with IBD, but typically lacks rapid weight loss and profound fatigue unless advanced or complicated by dominant stricture or cholangiocarcinoma; its chronicity makes it slightly less likely over a one-month timeframe. Autoimmune hepatitis with PBC overlap is possible given AMA relevance (though not yet tested), but usually presents with more prominent pruritus, elevated ALP/GGT, and less acute weight loss. Hepatocellular carcinoma is less likely without known cirrhosis or chronic viral hepatitis, though it can cause obstructive jaundice via portal invasion or mass effect — but weight loss and fatigue are more insidious. AMA status and cross-sectional imaging would critically refine this list: AMA+ strongly favors PBC; a discrete pancreatic head mass on CT/MRI would elevate pancreatic adenocarcinoma to >0.95 confidence."}
